name: Julie Lippert
fact: Lippert, a Paducah junior, was WKU homecoming queen for 1983, crowned at the Morehead game by the 1982 queen Mary Beth DeCastro; Lambda Chi Alpha and Alpha Gamma Rho sponsored her candidacy. She was Administrative Vice-President of Associated Student Government the following year.

name: Shiela Marie Waninger
fact: Waninger was president of the Phi Mu chapter at Western in 1982-83, the year before she sat in the Congress as alternate for the College of Education. The Talisman describes her as a junior from Fulda, Indiana, and quotes her on the chapter’s recruiting: the volume spells her first name Shelia.

name: Alan Jackson
kind: SEARCHED, NOT FOUND - no portrait exists in reach
fact: Alan Lawrence Jackson sat for no class portrait in any volume that could hold him, and the two photographs the archive does reach both hide his face. The 1980 Talisman index gives him exactly two pages, 'Jackson, Alan Lawrence 124, 423'. Printed p. 423 is a 'Student teacher' feature whose caption reads that helping kids with their social studies at McNeill Elementary School is part of sophomore Alan Jackson's contribution to tutoring efforts for his fraternity: the frame holds two elementary-school children facing the camera and one figure in the foreground with the back of the head to the lens, which is the tutor, so his face is not in the picture. Printed p. 124 is the Halloween spread, and its caption on p. 125 names five studio subjects, Molly and Betsy Bogdan, Alan Jackson, Candy Bush and Kathleen Hancock. He is the only man of the five and the p. 124 right-hand frame is the only man on the page, so the identification is sound, but the whole point of the frame is a Hallowe'en skull mask and makeup covering the face. The 1981 index lists him with no page numbers at all, so he is in no photograph in that volume. The 1982 index gives him one page, 'Jackson, Alan Lawrence 266', the Kappa Alpha Psi pledging feature 'Step in line' on pp. 266-267, where he is named twice in the body and once in a caption as the owner of the apartment the picture was taken in, and is in none of the four photographs. He was a senior that year, so the 1982 volume is his last chance at a grid cell and he is not in it. Corroboration that this is the right man and not a namesake: the 1980 caption calls him a Tampa, Fla., sophomore, the 1982 body text a Plant City, Fla., senior (two towns twenty miles apart in the same county, and the class years line up), and he is a Kappa Alpha Psi brother, which fits the Chair of Minority Affairs. Note that the 1982 caption on p. 266 calls him a Paducah senior, contradicting its own body text on the same page.
